_source: docs/content-bible.md §7 gym 1 (Maribel, Beast) — enemy party transcribed from data/gyms.json, as amended (Maribel reduced to three; her signature levels at +0). tests/unit/battle.test.ts re-reads gyms.json and fails if this party ever drifts from it, so the recording below cannot go stale in silence. build-doc §11: "fixtures/battle-scripts/*.json (action logs incl. gym fights)".
_replay: Headless: startBattle(input, ctx) then step(state, actions[i], rng, ctx) in order. `rngScript` is the deterministic float source the recording used, cycled; when core/rng.ts lands, drive the same script from the seeded battle stream (`seed` below) and re-record.
_foodWeb: Derived, not authored: deriveFoodWeb(toEcoNode(data/nodes/<id>.json), indexSpecies(species), balance) from core/foodweb.ts (G3 — battle.ts never derives an edge itself). It is recorded here so the fixture replays byte-identically; tests/unit/battle.test.ts re-derives it and fails if the EDGES ever drift. The comparison is by set, not by array order: predationOracleFromWebs folds both lists into Sets, so the order core/foodweb.ts emits them in changes no answer and is not part of the contract.
description: Year-1 gym: a six-strong Meadow party (Skir, Nibbin, Bramblehog, Pollywisp, Loamunder and a juvenile Cindril) against Maribel's Bramblehog/Skir and the Elder signature "Old Nib".

expect._reRecordedForT10T11: RE-RECORDED for T-10 + T-11. balance.age.multiplier was halved (J 0.75 -> 0.875, E 1.15 -> 1.075) and the Producer role template re-spent (atk 40 -> 60, ins 60 -> 40), so this party walks through Maribel faster than it used to: turns 12 -> 8, events 65 -> 47, eventDigest 51887e64 -> e397616b, and the last six commands had nothing left to hit. Those six are dropped on the same rule the 2026-08-25 re-recording used -- a fixture that records a refusal is not a recording of play -- so the action log is the SAME walk-through, ten commands instead of sixteen. The outcome is still `win` and the enemy party is still gyms.json's, which the test re-reads. p-polly and p-loam now end above zero because the fight ends before they are worn down, and p-loam is never sent out at all. Re-recorded, not loosened: every expectation below came out of replaying this file through core/battle.ts, and the digest is still exact.
expect._reRecordedForLevelCoefficientAndDivisor: RE-RECORDED for stats.levelCoefficient 0.02 -> 0.1 (Hank's ruling, 'as a temporary fix, just switch the level coefficient to be 0.1') AND for the NEW damage.divisor 1 -> 4, the term added to core/battle.ts that ties hit size to HP size (data/balance.json damage._divisor carries the measurement that chose 4). THE ACTION LOG HAD TO GROW, and that is the honest headline: every hit is now about a quarter of the size, so the ten recorded commands no longer finish the fight -- replayed verbatim they leave the battle UNRESOLVED (outcome null) at turn 11 with only maribel-1 down. A fixture that records an unfinished fight is not a recording of a gym win. THE WALK-THROUGH IS UNCHANGED AND THE EXTENSION RULE IS MECHANICAL, not hand-tuned: the recorded plan is read as an ordered walk-through of which creature is sent out and which move it throws -- p-skir/squall, p-nib/maul, p-brambl/overgrow, p-polly/overgrow -- and each creature simply keeps swinging until it either drops the leader's whole roster or is knocked out itself, at which point the walk-through moves to the next creature. No move and no creature is chosen here that the recorded log did not already choose; only the COUNT changes. 10 actions -> 21 (11 squall, switch to p-nib, 9 maul). turns 8 -> 20, events 47 -> 106, eventDigest 0a0cfff6 -> 8e2a54d0. WHAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE RE-RECORDING, because a digest nobody read is indistinguishable from laundering a regression: the pre-change state was reproduced exactly by replaying this file against an in-memory balance at levelCoefficient 0.02 / divisor 1, which returned outcome win, turns 8, events 47 and digest 0a0cfff6 -- byte-identical to what was recorded here -- so the old-vs-new diff below is trustworthy. Under the ORIGINAL ten commands nothing about the fight changed except arithmetic: no event kind appeared or disappeared and no outcome flipped; the damage amounts fell by roughly four (maribel-1's first hit 90 -> 27, p-skir's reply 59 -> 11) and the fight simply ran past the end of the log. The re-recorded 21-command version still ends in a win, still knocks out all three of Maribel's slots, and still puts a fainted player creature on the field mid-fight (p-skir, which is why finalHp reads 0 for it). p-brambl and p-polly are now never sent out -- p-nib mops up -- which is the one coverage loss and is recorded here rather than left to be discovered. No actionRejected is produced, as before.

_recording: RE-RECORDED 2026-08-25 against the amended roster. The action log is the SAME party walk-through as before, minus the two Maul commands that the shorter fight left with nothing to hit (they would have been refused with `actionRejected`, and a fixture that records a refusal is not a recording of play). Every expectation below — turns, event count, digest, final HP — was produced by replaying this file through core/battle.ts, not edited by hand.
